# King of Freight Expands to Colorado Springs, Creating New Job Opportunities

Wichita-Based Logistics Company Opens New Office, Plans to Hire 100 Employees by End of 2026

WICHITA, KS / September 22, 2026 / King of Freight, a Wichita, Kansas-based logistics company, is expanding its footprint with a new office opening today in Colorado Springs, Colorado, creating new job opportunities in the region.

The new location marks a significant step in King of Freight’s growth strategy, with the company aiming to hire 100 employees at the Colorado Springs office by the end of 2026. The expansion reflects continued demand for the company’s logistics and freight services beyond its Kansas home base.

"Opening our Colorado Springs office is about more than growing our footprint. It’s about bringing new job opportunities to a new community. We’re excited to build a strong local team here and continue the same commitment to our people that has driven our growth from the start," said a King of Freight spokesperson.

# Wagner Logistics to Add Nearly 80 Jobs with New High-Volume Logistics Operation in Liberty

 Wagner Logistics 

Oct 14, 2026, 08:54 ET

NORTH KANSAS CITY, Mo., Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Wagner Logistics, a nationwide provider of third-party logistics, today announced it has signed a multi-year agreement with a Kansas City-area manufacturer to launch a new manufacturing support and warehouse operations program in Liberty, Mo.

The new operation includes two leased warehouse facilities in the Liberty area totaling more than 830,000 square feet. Wagner expects to add 79 new local jobs over the next two years, starting immediately. The company will also make a multi-million-dollar investment in equipment, infrastructure and automated trailer loading and unloading technology to support the operation.

"This is exactly the kind of operation where Wagner's strengths come through," said Brian Smith, President and Chief Executive Officer of Wagner Logistics. "It requires speed, flexibility, close coordination and the ability to design a solution around what the customer actually needs."

Two new LTL facilities in Arizona and Missouri extend XPO's North American footprint as the carrier invests in capacity ahead of expected freight recovery.

 By Tess Crawford, Markets, Rates, Fuel & Carrier Business · 4 min read · October 6, 2026 

 Photo: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons) 

## Why is XPO opening new service centers now?

XPO opened two LTL service centers on October 5, 2026, one in Mesa, Arizona, and one in Cameron, Missouri. The facilities are part of a broader capital investment in the carrier's North American network, adding door capacity and geographic reach at a time when most LTL carriers are running sub-95% utilization and spot truckload rates remain soft.

The timing reflects XPO's bet that freight volume will recover before competitors finish adding capacity. The carrier has been posting sequential tonnage gains since Q1 2026, when LTL revenue rose 5% year-over-year to $1.23 billion on slight tonnage growth and a 4% yield gain excluding fuel.
